title: metsuke v1 — SPO telemetry build
description:
Build epic for the metsuke v1 telemetry pipeline: SPO agent (scrape, spool, sign, upload) and ingest server (verify, archive to S3), per /tmp/metsuke-spec.md collapsed from wayfinder map musashi-ping-sak (decision phase; all 15 map tickets closed). Decision detail lives in musashi-ping-sak.1–15 and docs/research/; accepted decisions in docs/adr/0001–0007. Scaffolding is done and green — tickets start from a working workspace.

## Success Criteria

- An SPO can follow the instructions page from zero to verified uploads: static binary, hardened unit, cold-key or Calidus signing.
- The server verifies, replay-protects, and archives every accepted submission raw in S3; the index is rebuildable from a bucket listing.
- nix flake check stays hermetic and green; the VM test proves the full path on hydraJobs.

title: Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core
description:
## What to build

The shared wire contract both crates trust: envelope types (schema_version starting at 1, pool_id, agent_version, replay counter, timestamp, samples with the 8 nullable v1 fields), zstd compression, and raw detached Ed25519 sign/verify over the compressed body bytes (ADR 0001). Exposed as a library from the metsuke crate so the server consumes the identical types and defaults — reviewers verify one definition, not two copies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Property test: envelope encode→decode roundtrip.
- [ ] Property test: sign→verify roundtrip, and any tampered byte in the compressed body rejects.
- [ ] Replay counter and timestamp sit inside the signed payload (ADR 0002).
- [ ] metsuke-server can depend on the metsuke crate as a library.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
close_reason: seal/open wire core with property tests; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: envelope schema v1 (PoolId opaque type, 8 nullable sample fields) with seal/open as the whole wire interface — seal = JSON+zstd+Ed25519 sign, open = verify_strict before bounded decompress (ADR 0001/0002). Property tests: seal→open roundtrip, tamper rejects, PoolId bech32 roundtrip; unit tests for size cap, NaN, malformed/wrong-prefix/wrong-length pool ids. Server depends on metsuke by path; crate versions decoupled per ADR 0006. Filed metsuke-9a1 (deferred metsuke-wire extraction).

title: Developer data endpoints
description:
## What to build

Developer pull access to the archive without per-dev AWS credentials: a single basic-auth user (credentials via sops EnvironmentFile), a listing route (prefix and after filters, JSON from the SQLite index) and a download route streaming the raw S3 object. Read-only, no transformation — developers get the same self-verifying bytes the bucket holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing or wrong credentials → 401 on both routes.
- [ ] Listing filters by prefix and after; results come from the index, not a live bucket scan.
- [ ] Download streams the object byte-identical to what was archived.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index.

title: Instructions page
description:
## What to build

The SPO onboarding surface: one static HTML page (no JS, no CSS effort) rendered at server build time from a template whose every code-owned value — intervals, port, flake output names, latest client version, the exact field list that leaves the box — is pulled from the client crate at compile, so documentation can never drift from shipped defaults (ADR 0006). Outline per musashi-ping-sak.14: intro and fields, register, choose signing key, enable PrometheusSimple, install, configure, systemd, verify, staying up to date. Numbered copy-paste steps take an SPO from zero to verified uploads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Page builds from client-crate constants; changing a default in code changes the page with no manual edit.
- [ ] The exact v1 field list appears on the page.
- [ ] All outline sections present, each step copy-pasteable.
- [ ] Served by the ingest server as static content.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end; Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.

title: Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit
description:
## What to build

Distribution as declared in the spec — Nix-flake-only, no install script ever: static musl flake outputs metsuke-static-x86_64-linux and metsuke-static-aarch64-linux cross-built via crane, a NixOS module for the agent and one for the server (all spec limits exposed as module options, never hardcoded), and an example hardened unit at contrib/metsuke.service (DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, StateDirectory, no groups — ADR 0007) with the LoadCredential variant documented as optional.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both static outputs build; binaries link no dynamic libraries.
- [ ] Agent module renders config TOML from options; server module exposes every limit as an option.
- [ ] contrib unit committed; agent runs under it against a loopback endpoint with no extra privileges.
- [ ] nix flake check remains hermetic and green.

## Blocked by

Client binary end-to-end.

title: Server SQLite backup timer
description:
## What to build

Recovery for the index between rebuilds: a systemd timer in the server NixOS module running roughly hourly — sqlite3 .backup, zstd, aws s3 cp into a backups/ prefix in the same bucket, using the server's existing scoped credentials. Complements (does not replace) the rebuild-from-listing path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Timer and service rendered by the server module; cadence is an option.
- [ ] Backup is a consistent snapshot (sqlite3 .backup, not a file copy), compressed, uploaded under backups/.
- [ ] Failure surfaces in the journal; it never blocks ingest.

## Blocked by

Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

title: NixOS VM end-to-end test
description:
## What to build

The one non-hermetic sanity gate (hydraJobs only, never in nix flake check): a NixOS VM test wiring a real idle Leios node (pinned via the ouroboros-leios prototype tag input, not capkgs), the real agent via its module, the real server via its module, and Garage as S3. Asserts the full path — scrape → spool → signed upload → verify → S3 object → ACK — once; moving values stay covered by tier-2 fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VM test passes: an object appears in Garage and the agent logs the ACK.
- [ ] Runs from hydraJobs; excluded from nix flake check (which stays no-node, no-VM, no-network).
- [ ] Leios pin is a flake input, bumpable with the fixture re-record flow.

## Blocked by

S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index; Static builds, NixOS modules, hardened unit.

title: Bucket and IAM in cardano-playground
description:
## What to build

External-repo infrastructure (cardano-playground, not this repo): the cardano-playground-metsuke bucket in the opentofu bootstrap (SSE-KMS via the shared key alias, versioning, TLS-only policy, access logging, public access blocked) and the IT-security-approved dedicated IAM user — PutObject/GetObject/ListBucket on this one bucket plus KMS decrypt/generate scoped to the alias — with static keys in a sops EnvironmentFile readable only by the metsuke systemd user on the db-sync host. Blocks production deploy only; the VM test uses Garage and does not wait on this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bucket applied with all five protections listed above.
- [ ] IAM policy grants nothing beyond the one bucket and the scoped KMS actions.
- [ ] Credentials land via sops, readable only by the service user.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately (gates production deploy, not other tickets).

title: HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs is still `println!("metsuke-server")`. Nothing loads IngestConfig (no TOML/env loader), binds a socket, or constructs Intake.

Needs: config load, listener, POST route reading the ADR-0001 headers into Submission, and the status mapping IngestError already implies — IngestError::Rejected -> 4xx with the Rejection text, CounterState/Archive -> 5xx (ADR 0004, so the client keeps spooling).

metsuke-4zo.6 delivered the intake library; .7 assumes a 503 path exists. No ticket owned this layer.
close_reason: HTTP ingest endpoint, config loader, and server binary wiring

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review — HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring

### Silent failures

- `src/http.rs:249-259` — `serve()` treats a dead listener as a dropped connection. tiny_http 0.12 pushes `Message::Error` and `break`s out of its accept thread when `accept()` fails (lib.rs:341-345), so `recv()` yields that error exactly once and every later call blocks forever on an empty queue. The process stays alive, logs `dropped a connection` once, and accepts nothing again; systemd sees a healthy unit. Fix: make `serve` return `Result<Infallible, io::Error>`, propagate the recv error to `main`, exit nonzero.
- `src/http.rs:249-339` — nothing bounds how long a body read may take, and the loop is single-threaded, so one client that sends headers then stalls wedges ingest for every pool. `read_body` bounds size, not time. Fix: set a read timeout on the connection, or state in the module header that the fronting proxy must fully buffer request bodies and file that requirement against the NixOS module ticket (metsuke-4zo.12).

### Prose claims

- `src/http.rs:1-4` — "any IP-level limit belong to the reverse proxy … see docs/research/endpoint-protection.md §4". §4 is Transport (TLS only); IP and rate limiting are §3 step 3 and §5. Fix: cite §3 and §5 for the limit half of the claim.
- `src/http.rs:225-227` — retells ADR-0004 and drifts from it: the comment calls 4xx "permanent", ADR-0004 says on 4xx the client keeps the data spooled and retries with clamped exponential backoff. Fix: cut to a pointer, `// Status family only; ADR 0004 defines what each means to the client.`
- `src/config.rs:92-93` — "The S3 archive (ticket metsuke-4zo.7) replaces it" is a third copy; `src/archive.rs:1-3` and `:12-13` already own that fact. Fix: drop the ticket clause.

### Ambiguity

Ticket says "no TOML/env loader"; only TOML is loaded. Was an env source required, or was that phrasing just naming what was absent?

### Gates run this session

`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean. `cargo test` — 100 passed, 0 failed (11 in metsuke-server/tests/binary.rs, 9 in tests/http.rs, 4 in tests/config.rs). `nix flake check` not run.

### Beads hygiene

No untracked files; every change is staged. `br sync --status`: in sync, 0 dirty. Ticket has no resolution comment and is still in_progress — yours to close. Map metsuke-4zo has no Decisions/Out-of-scope sections, so nothing to update there.

### Filed

Commented on metsuke-9a1 (cross-crate duplication: ERR/WARNING/INFO, `hex`, three hex decoders, the `Args::parse` loop).

### Verdict

Not ready for /commit: the listener-death path and the missing body-read bound need a decision first. The three prose fixes are cheap.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review 2 — HTTP ingest endpoint and server binary wiring

All five findings from the first review are addressed: `serve` returns `Result<Infallible, io::Error>` and `main` exits FAILURE; the body-timeout requirement is documented in the http.rs header and filed as metsuke-a3a; the endpoint-protection citation now names sections that exist; the ADR-0004 retelling is a pointer; the 4zo.7 clause is gone from config.rs.

### Correctness

- `src/http.rs:read_body` — the Content-Length shortcut does not avoid the cost it claims to. Refusing without reading leaves the remainder for tiny_http's `EqualReader::drop`, which allocates `vec![0; declared_content_length]` on the serving thread. Measured: one header-only POST declaring `Content-Length: 4000000000`, answered 400, took the process from VmSize 347544 kB to 4253796 kB. Detail and the fix are on metsuke-a3a. In this diff, fix the comment: the check saves verification work, not reading.

### Prose claims

- `src/http.rs` `decode_hex` doc — "ADR 0001 fixes what the client emits" is not in ADR 0001, which says only that "HTTP headers carry pool id, verification key, and signature" and specifies no hex encoding or casing. What actually fixes it is `crates/metsuke/src/uploader.rs` `fn hex` (lowercase). Fix: name that, drop the ADR citation.

### Logging

- `src/http.rs:respond` and `refuse` — a failed `respond` is logged at WARNING and dropped. tiny_http already maps BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset to `Ok`, so what reaches this branch is a real write failure on a submission already archived with its counter spent: the agent never sees the ACK, resends, and gets 400 `does not advance`. Neither line names the pool. Fix: log this one at ERR, and put the claimed pool id in both messages.

### Open question

Ticket says "no TOML/env loader"; only TOML is loaded. Was an env source required, or was that phrasing naming what was absent? Asked in review 1, unanswered.

### Gates run this session

`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — clean. `cargo test --workspace` — 100 passed, 0 failed. `nix flake check` not run.

### Beads hygiene

No untracked files; every change staged. Ticket still in_progress with no resolution comment — yours to close. Map metsuke-4zo has no Decisions/Out-of-scope sections. The cross-crate duplication (ERR/WARNING/INFO, `hex`, three hex decoders, the `Args::parse` loop) is already on metsuke-9a1 from review 1; re-confirmed, nothing new to file. `.beads/issues.jsonl` needs re-staging after this flush.

### Verdict

Three fixes, all small and none blocking a decision: the read_body comment, the ADR-0001 hex citation, and the respond/refuse log level and pool id.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
HTTP ingest layer shipped: src/http.rs (SUBMIT_PATH, SubmissionHeaders::decode over the ADR-0001 headers, status_for, bounded read_body, serve), src/cli.rs (--config), ServerConfig in src/config.rs (listen, counters_path, archive_root, [ingest]; no defaults), main.rs wiring, Intake::max_body_bytes().

tiny_http 0.12, no default features: a sync accept loop matches Intake's &mut self plus rusqlite; 3 crates added. serve returns Result<Infallible, io::Error> and exits nonzero because tiny_http abandons its accept thread on the first accept failure, so a logged-and-continued error would look healthy while accepting nothing.

Status map: 413 oversize, 429 rate-limited, 403 unknown pool / wrong key / bad signature, 400 other client faults, 503 counter store and archive (ADR 0004).

Config is TOML only, no env source: env limits would be a second home for numbers config.toml owns.

25 tests: tests/http.rs (9, header decode), tests/binary.rs (11, spawned binary over a real socket), tests/config.rs (4, every field required). nix flake check green.

Filed metsuke-a3a: a trickled request body stalls all ingest, and tiny_http drains the declared Content-Length on drop; both need the fronting proxy that metsuke-4zo.12 owns.

title: spool migrate() silently opens a future schema
description:
crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:57 — `.skip(applied as usize)` yields an empty iterator when user_version > MIGRATIONS.len(), so migrate() returns Ok and an old binary runs against a schema it does not know.

Fix: error when applied > MIGRATIONS.len(), naming both numbers.

Pre-existing; the same hole was copied into crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs by metsuke-4zo.6 and is fixed there in scope.
close_reason: Fixed by the shared metsuke::sqlite::migrate guard

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Fixed in metsuke-4zo.6: migrate() moved to metsuke::sqlite with the applied > migrations.len() guard, so spool.rs and the server counter store share it. Covered by metsuke-server/tests/counters.rs a_database_from_a_newer_build_fails_loudly. Close with .6's commit.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Implemented by metsuke-4zo.6's diff: crates/metsuke/src/sqlite.rs:21-26 refuses a database whose user_version exceeds the migration list (MigrateError::FromTheFuture), and both spool.rs and counters.rs now call that shared migrate(). Close this once .6 lands.

title: scrape test races for a released MockServer port
description:
crates/metsuke/tests/scrape.rs:77 `unreachable_endpoint_yields_all_nulls` starts a MockServer, drops it, and assumes the port stays dead. Another test's MockServer takes the freed port and serves a chain body, so the sample comes back populated.

Observed red in 2 of 4 runs on the metsuke-4zo.6 tree (`cargo test --workspace` and `nix flake check`, one each); both retries passed.

Fix: point at an address nothing can reclaim (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, as tests/uploader.rs does) instead of racing for a released one.
close_reason: unreachable scrape test now targets TEST-NET-1 instead of a reclaimable port

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Reproduces on the metsuke-4zo.6 working tree, not a one-off: 2 of 4 runs red this session. `cargo test --workspace` failed it once then passed 84/0; `nix flake check` failed it once (node_version/node_revision came back populated from another test's MockServer) then passed. It is the only thing standing between this tree and a green gate — worth raising from P3.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Replaced the released-MockServer-port trick with 192.0.2.1:9 (TEST-NET-1) and a 200ms timeout in unreachable_endpoint_yields_all_nulls. cargo test --workspace green x3; nix flake check: all checks passed.

title: Prometheus scrape into a sample
description:
## What to build

The agent turns one scrape of the node's loopback PrometheusSimple endpoint into one sample: the 8 v1 fields, node version/revision parsed from the build_info labelled metric, every field nullable because a failed scrape is itself signal (ADR 0007). Fixtures are cassette recordings of real Leios node bodies replayed via wiremock, with a committed re-record script — so review can trust the parser matches Leios metric names, not stock cardano-node assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recorded Leios scrape body in → sample with correct field values out.
- [ ] Unreachable endpoint or missing metric → sample with nulls, no error path taken.
- [ ] Hand-authored edge-case fixtures live visibly separate from recordings.
- [ ] Re-record script committed; fixtures documented to refresh on Leios flake-input bumps.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (sample type lives in the envelope).
close_reason: scrape into sample with real Leios cassettes; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: scrape.rs turning one PrometheusSimple scrape into one Sample, infallible (failures degrade to nulls per ADR 0007). Metric names frozen against real cassettes recorded from a lone forging Leios node at the flake-pinned prototype tag; startup body doubles as the real missing-metric fixture. Hand-authored edge cases separate under edge-cases/. Re-record script scripts/record-scrape-fixtures.sh committed and exercised end-to-end. 9 wiremock tests; flake source filter keeps .prom files. Filed metsuke-ixn (sync_progress has no source metric); noted on metsuke-9a1 that its extraction trigger fired.

title: SNTP clock-offset probe
description:
## What to build

A per-sample SNTP query filling clock_offset_ms: single code path, configurable server list, shipped default time.cloudflare.com, null on probe failure. No timedatectl fallback — one path keeps the attack surface and the review surface small.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Offset computed from an SNTP exchange against a test server.
- [ ] Server list is configuration; default is time.cloudflare.com.
- [ ] Probe failure yields a null offset, not an aborted sample.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (field lives in the sample type).
close_reason: SNTP probe + sampler merge; scripted-UDP tests; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: sntp module — hand-rolled RFC 4330 SNTP v4 over std UdpSocket (no new dep), probe(&SntpConfig) -> Option<i64>, servers tried in order, reply validation (originate echo, mode 4, stratum != 0, LI != 3, >= 48 bytes), failure -> None. Review round 1 added sampler::sample() owning scrape + probe + merge. Tests: 9 scripted-UDP-server SNTP tests plus a wiremock+UDP seam test; clippy deny-warnings, workspace tests, nix flake check all green.

title: SQLite spool
description:
## What to build

The agent's only durability layer (ADR 0004): one rusqlite DB owning samples, delivery state, and schema migrations. Rows are deleted only on server ACK; all outstanding rows retry at startup and every upload interval; a configurable size cap bounds growth. Correctness here is what makes "nothing is lost across restarts or server downtime" true, so the tests are the review artifact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Property test: write→ack→delete leaves no orphan rows in any state table.
- [ ] Restart with undelivered rows → they are offered for upload again.
- [ ] Size cap is configuration and is enforced.
- [ ] Schema migrations run on open; fresh DB and migrated DB behave identically.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core (spool stores envelope samples).
close_reason: SQLite spool + delivery seam; all four acceptance criteria tested

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: spool.rs (SQLite durability layer: migrations via user_version, transactional push with configured max_samples oldest-drop, outstanding oldest-first, transactional ack, durable replay counter) and delivery.rs from review (take_batch seals outstanding rows into a SealedBatch holding row ids privately; ack consumes the batch). 10 tests incl. write→ack→delete orphan property test (mutation-checked) and restart durability.

title: Client binary end-to-end
description:
## What to build

The complete agent an SPO runs: TOML config (pool_id, metrics_url, upload_url, optional signing_key; interval/SNTP defaults commented), key resolution --signing-key flag > config path > loud failure (systemd LoadCredential support), a 5-minute sample loop and a decoupled 1-hour upload loop (both configurable) that compresses, signs, and POSTs batches with pool_id/vkey/signature headers. 5xx or network failure keeps spooling and retries next interval with jitter; 4xx keeps the spool, logs the server's reason to journald, and backs off exponentially with a clamp; an ACK carrying a newer latest_version logs a journal warning. Demoable end-to-end against a wiremock server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recorded scrape bodies in → signed, compressed batch with correct headers out (external-behaviour test).
- [ ] Missing key at both flag and config → startup fails loudly.
- [ ] 5xx: spool intact, retry scheduled with jitter. 4xx: spool intact, reason logged, backoff clamped.
- [ ] ACK deletes the delivered rows; newer latest_version in the ACK logs a warning.
- [ ] Sample and upload cadences are independent configuration.

## Blocked by

Prometheus scrape into a sample; SNTP clock-offset probe; SQLite spool.
close_reason: client binary end-to-end; 32 tests incl. binary-level; flake check green

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped: config.rs (TOML, required fields loud, all limits defaulted knobs, example config pinned by test), keys.rs (TextEnvelope 5820 seed, flag>config>loud failure), cli.rs (hand-parsed --config/--signing-key), uploader.rs (ADR-0001 headers, Acked/Retryable/Rejected + ADR-0006 nudge), schedule.rs (pure: jitter on retryable, clamped exponential backoff on 4xx), agent.rs ticks, main.rs loop with journald severity prefixes. Delivery now takes pool_id from config (Calidus, ADR 0003). Review round 1: split AckAfterAccept error, binary-level tests incl. mutation-checked flag>config precedence, tests/support module, prose fixes. Filed metsuke-oqh.

title: Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path
description:
## What to build

The ingest server accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end. Checks run cheap→expensive: allowlist → per-pool rate limit → Ed25519 verify over the compressed bytes → bounded streaming decompression (fixed arena) → replay-counter check — verification precedes decompression so only authenticated bytes reach the decompressor (ADR 0002). Cold-key identity is pure computation: blake2b-224(vkey) == pool_id (ADR 0003). Accepted submissions go to storage behind a trait with a filesystem implementation (the cargo-test seam); the ACK carries latest_version embedded from the client crate at build. Every limit is configuration, never a constant. Rejections carry a reason the client can log.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid signed batch in → stored object (raw bytes as received) + ACK with latest_version out.
- [ ] Each check rejects independently with a distinct reason: oversized body, unknown pool, rate limit, unauthorized key, bad signature, oversized decompression, unsupported schema version, envelope pool id not the submitted one, timestamp outside the window, stale/replayed counter.
- [ ] Property test: replay-counter acceptance logic (monotonic per pool, state in SQLite).
- [ ] Decompression never allocates beyond its configured ceiling.
- [ ] No check reads decompressed bytes before signature verification passes.

## Blocked by

Envelope and Ed25519 sign/verify core.
close_reason: Intake library green; HTTP wiring split to .16

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Review of .4 (O3): build ingest as one intake module — single entry point taking raw bytes + signature, returning accepted-envelope-or-rejection with one exhaustive error type; key store, counter store, archive as adapters behind it. Keeps the four-ADR ordering out of main.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review of the working tree (report-only)

Gates run this session: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 100 passed 0 failed; `nix flake check` all checks passed. No untracked files — every new file is staged, so the flake gate saw them.

### Intent

- crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:1 — no HTTP layer, no config loader, main is still a stub, so 'the ingest server accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end' holds only at library level. Filed metsuke-4zo.16; decide whether .6 closes on the library or absorbs .16.
- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:189 — 'Decompression never allocates beyond its configured ceiling' is not met: read_to_end doubles a growing Vec, so peak capacity reaches ~2x the ceiling. Fix: Vec::with_capacity(max+1) before read_to_end.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:443-461 — counter advances before archive.store, ADR-0002 says counter state 'is updated only after the full chain passes'. The code comment argues for the current order; that argument belongs in the ADR. Either reorder or amend ADR-0002.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:418-430 — UnsupportedSchema and PoolIdMismatch are not in the ticket's check chain or ADR-0002. PoolIdMismatch closes a real gap (allowlist and rate limit run on the header, not the signed body). Keep, add both to the ticket's reason list and to ADR-0002's chain.

### Standards

- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:187-194 — migrate() is byte-identical to crates/metsuke/src/spool.rs:57-63. Extract one `migrate(conn, migrations)` into the metsuke crate; each caller keeps its own `#[from] rusqlite::Error`.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:189 — `.skip(applied as usize)` returns Ok when user_version > MIGRATIONS.len(), so an old binary opens a newer schema silently. Error naming both numbers. Same hole pre-exists in spool.rs: metsuke-4zo.17.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:286 — Submission.body vs wire_bytes everywhere else (envelope::open, SealedBatch.wire_bytes, StoredSubmission.wire_bytes); intake.rs:460 copies one into the other. Rename the field to wire_bytes.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:36-37 — 'so the stored object re-verifies on its own' is false for FilesystemArchive, which writes only wire_bytes; vkey, signature and schema_version on StoredSubmission are read by no code. ADR-0005's metadata headers and index row belong to metsuke-4zo.7. Cite .7 where the fields are declared, or drop the claim.

### Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:1-5 — restates ADR-0002's check ordering verbatim. ADR-0002 owns it; keep the pointer only.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/archive.rs:1-2 — restates ADR-0005's 'zstd bytes exactly as received'. Same.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/counters.rs:177-178 — restates spool.rs:45's migration-convention sentence. Point at metsuke::spool.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/lib.rs:5-8 — the parenthetical module map repeats what the five `pub mod` lines below say. Drop it.

### Discarded

Rate limit charged before the cold-key check is the order ADR-0002 documents. RateLimiter's HashMap is bounded by the allowlist, since the allowlist check precedes it. u64-as-i64 casts and the duplicated all-sevens test seed do not clear the bar.

### Filed

metsuke-4zo.16, metsuke-4zo.17.

### Beads hygiene

.beads/issues.jsonl is modified and unstaged — stage it with the code. Ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason yet; the map's Success Criteria section carries no per-ticket decision line.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Review of the working tree (report-only, second pass)

Gates run this session: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean.
`cargo test --workspace` — one run failed `metsuke --test scrape`, the rerun
passed 84/0. `nix flake check` — one run failed the same test, the rerun said
"all checks passed". That is metsuke-4zo.18, 2 of 4 runs red on this tree; the
evidence is on .18 now. No untracked files, so the flake gate sees every new
file.

The four findings from the first pass that were fixed are gone from this report:
the shared `migrate()`, its future-schema guard, the decompression arena, and
`Submission.wire_bytes`.

### Intent

- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:190-192 — the arena fix overshot: every `open`
  now commits `max_decompressed_bytes` up front, so the configured ceiling
  became a per-request floor. A 200-byte payload reserves the full ceiling, and
  once metsuke-4zo.16 serves this concurrently it is N × ceiling of RSS. Read
  `decoder.take(max+1)` into a fixed chunk buffer and `reserve_exact` per chunk
  — capacity then tracks real data and still never passes the ceiling.
- crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs:191,194 — `saturating_add(1)` for the arena but
  plain `max_decompressed_bytes + 1` for `take`, and the `usize::try_from` is an
  `.expect()`. An operator config value should not panic the request path.
  One saturating value for both, and an `OpenError` variant instead of the
  expect.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:474-495 — `archive.store` precedes
  `counters.accept`, so a submission that loses the counter race is stored and
  then rejected. Two racing bodies at one counter share an object key, so the
  archive can end up holding the loser's bytes while the ACK went to the
  winner. Either put the store and the counter write in one transaction, or
  state in ADR-0002 that a stored-but-rejected object is the accepted cost.
- crates/metsuke/src/sqlite.rs:21-26 — this is metsuke-4zo.17's fix, done
  inside .6. Commented on .17; close it with this work or the work is
  untracked.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/main.rs:1 — still `println!`, so "the ingest server
  accepting its first authenticated submission end-to-end" holds at library
  level only. metsuke-4zo.16 owns the HTTP layer; decide whether .6 closes on
  the library or absorbs .16.

### Standards

- crates/metsuke-server/src/config.rs:16 — "Cap on the compressed body, checked
  before anything reads it" is false: intake.rs:95 measures
  `submission.wire_bytes.len()`, a slice already fully buffered. Say that .16
  owns the streaming cap, or the comment claims protection the code has not
  got.
- crates/metsuke-server/src/ratelimit.rs:31-32 — "a rejected attempt is not
  charged, so a throttled pool cannot extend its own lockout by retrying": the
  window resets on elapsed time and `started_at` never moves on a charge, so
  charging could not extend anything. Drop the clause; the behaviour is right,
  the reason given for it is not.

### Prose

- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:113-115 — restates ADR-0003:18-19 ("the
  pool id *is* that hash. Pure computation, no infrastructure"). Keep the
  pointer and the Calidus note, drop the mechanism.
- crates/metsuke/src/lib.rs:4-5 — the ACK-embedding mechanics are already on
  the field at envelope.rs:23-24, which owns them. Shorten to "This agent
  build's version (ADR 0006)."
- crates/metsuke-server/src/intake.rs:189-190 — first sentence restates
  ADR-0002's amended decision text verbatim in substance. Cut it; the
  read-spares-the-PUT / write-settles-the-race sentence is local reasoning and
  stays.

### Discarded

`or_insert_with` in ratelimit, `create_dir_all` per store, the two `test_now()`
helpers (separate test binaries, and counters.rs:11-12 states why its instant
differs), `pool()` vs `pool_of`, unpadded counter in the object key,
`Intake::accept` naming, the twice-built `ReplayedCounter`, and the rustfmt
churn in binary.rs and uploader.rs.

### Filed

Commented on metsuke-4zo.17, metsuke-4zo.18. No new tickets.

### Beads hygiene

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is staged, and staged again after this comment — restage
before committing. The ticket has no resolution comment and no close reason.
The map metsuke-4zo has no `## Decisions so far` section to gain a line; its
Success Criteria block is untouched. Acceptance criterion 2 was rewritten by
this diff to add the five reasons the code implements, so that criterion now
matches the code by construction — worth a word in the resolution comment.

### Verdict

Not ready for `/commit`. Blocking: `nix flake check` is red on 2 of 4 runs via
metsuke-4zo.18, and the envelope.rs allocation regression should not ship as
the answer to the first pass.

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Shipped the intake library: one submit() running body cap, allowlist, per-pool rate limit, cold-key identity, Ed25519 verify, bounded decompression, schema/pool-id/timestamp cross-checks, replay counter. Archive behind a trait with a filesystem impl; counter reservation commits with the store. HTTP layer is metsuke-4zo.16.

title: S3 storage implementation and rebuildable index
description:
## What to build

The production storage trait impl (ADR 0005): one S3 object per accepted submission, raw signed zstd bytes exactly as received, key v1/<pool_id>/<date>/<unix_ts>-<counter>.json.zst, envelope metadata duplicated into x-amz-meta-* headers so the bucket is self-verifying. PUT is synchronous before ACK — no server spool — with a configurable timeout and one retry, then 503 so the client keeps spooling. The server SQLite row is only an index: an admin command rebuilds it from a bucket listing, making server disk loss recoverable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Object key and x-amz-meta-* headers carry signature, key, counter, schema_version.
- [ ] PUT failure after one retry → 503, nothing indexed, client-visible.
- [ ] Rebuild command reconstructs an equivalent index from a listing of the stored objects.
- [ ] Stored bytes are byte-identical to the received body (self-verifying corpus).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.

title: Calidus verification path
description:
## What to build

The second key path (ADR 0003), letting SPOs keep cold keys off the telemetry box: the upload vkey must match the pool's registered Calidus (label 867) key, resolved by SQL against the Leios db-sync, highest nonce wins, an all-zero key (CIP-151 revoke) rejects. Resolutions cache forever; a verification failure triggers exactly one fresh lookup and retry, rate-limited per pool, so db-sync sees no per-upload load and key rotation still converges.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Upload signed with the registered Calidus key verifies; unregistered key rejects.
- [ ] Highest-nonce registration wins; all-zero key rejects the pool's Calidus path.
- [ ] Cache hit performs no db-sync query; verify failure performs one refresh then re-verifies.
- [ ] Refresh-on-fail is rate-limited per pool (limit is configuration).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path.

title: Allowlist generation admin command
description:
## What to build

The admin command producing the participant gate: registration CSV ∩ active on-chain pool registrations carrying the matching CIP-20 label-674 key musashinet_incentives_application_code, queried from db-sync, emitted as (pool_id, code) pairs into Nix-managed server config. Codes are public and never treated as secrets; runtime stays db-sync-free on the cold-key path. The command is how operators onboard pools, so its output format is the server's allowlist input format by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CSV row with matching on-chain code → pair emitted; CSV-only or chain-only pools are excluded.
- [ ] Output loads directly as the ingest server's allowlist configuration.
- [ ] Emitted with a summary the operator can review (counts of matched/excluded).

## Blocked by

Server ingest pipeline, cold-key path (defines the allowlist it feeds).

title: Extract wire contract into metsuke-wire crate
description: crates/metsuke/src/envelope.rs is the wire contract; metsuke-server depends on the whole agent crate for it. Every future agent dep (HTTP, rusqlite, SNTP) becomes a server dep transitively, against least-privilege, and ADR 0006 independent versioning forces server manifest churn per client tag. Fix: move envelope.rs into a metsuke-wire crate both binaries depend on. Deliberately deferred from metsuke-4zo.1 review: do it when the first heavy agent dependency lands (metsuke-4zo.2/.4).

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
More cross-crate duplication for the extraction to absorb, found reviewing metsuke-4zo.16:

- journald severity prefixes: crates/metsuke/src/main.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO (private) vs crates/metsuke-server/src/lib.rs ERR/WARNING/INFO — byte-identical.
- lowercase hex encode: metsuke/src/uploader.rs `fn hex` (private) vs metsuke-server/tests/support/mod.rs `fn hex` — byte-identical.
- hex decode, three shapes: metsuke/src/keys.rs `decode_seed`, metsuke/tests/support/mod.rs `decode_hex`, metsuke-server/src/http.rs `decode_hex<const N>` (the best-shaped of the three).
- `Args::parse` loop: metsuke/src/cli.rs vs metsuke-server/src/cli.rs — same shape; the client's `value()` helper already generalises the flag-value case.

title: Slow request body stalls all ingest
description:
crates/metsuke-server/src/http.rs: serve() reads bodies on the accepting thread and tiny_http 0.12 exposes no socket timeout (ServerConfig is addr+ssl only; Request hands out no stream), so one client trickling a body blocks every pool until it gives up. read_body bounds size, not time.

Fix: front the server with a proxy that fully buffers request bodies, and bind loopback. Belongs with metsuke-4zo.12, which owns the NixOS modules and the hardened unit. If the endpoint is ever exposed directly, tiny_http has to go.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Same root cause, second cost: memory, not just time.

Any path that answers without reading the body (413 by Content-Length, 404, 405, header-decode 400) leaves the remainder unread, and tiny_http's EqualReader::drop drains it with a single `vec![0; remaining]` sized by the *declared* Content-Length (util/equal_reader.rs:66-85; the >1024 branch at request.rs:215). Request::drop runs it on the serving thread, and no public Request method lets you skip it (upgrade/into_writer/respond all drop self).

Measured, debug build, one header-only POST declaring Content-Length: 4000000000, answered 400: VmSize 347544 kB -> 4253796 kB, freed when the client closed. RSS stays ~4 MB (calloc zero pages) until the attacker actually sends bytes.

Consequence: under the hardened unit's MemoryMax/LimitAS (metsuke-4zo.12) this aborts the process. Fix is the same proxy body cap this ticket already names; the cap has to be enforced *before* the request reaches tiny_http.

title: Bump workspace to Rust edition 2024
description: Cargo.toml workspace.package pins edition 2021; toolchain is rustc 1.97 and committed style is already rustfmt style_edition 2024 (treefmt), so cargo fmt disagrees with the repo. Fix: edition = "2024" in Cargo.toml, re-run gates.
close_reason: edition 2024 in workspace Cargo.toml; envelope seal check rewritten as let-chain; gates green

title: sync_progress has no source metric on the Leios endpoint
description: crates/metsuke/src/scrape.rs: the Leios PrometheusSimple endpoint (recorded fixtures, prototype-2026w32) exposes no sync-progress metric, so the v1 scrape always leaves sync_progress null. Decide: drop the field from schema v1, or accept a permanently-null field until a source exists. Envelope field is metsuke-4zo.1 scope; scrape is metsuke-4zo.2.

title: Migrate pre-existing test-key copies to tests/support
description: crates/metsuke/tests/{delivery,wire,keys,sntp?}.rs each construct SigningKey::from_bytes(&[7u8; 32]) inline; tests/support/mod.rs (added in metsuke-4zo.5 review round 1) owns test_key(). Move the pre-existing copies over. Mechanical.
